 By Thanaaz Hisham My relationship with K-dramas is a little less straightforward than you might think. I’m the older sibling who has spent years discovering all the cooler things in life courtesy of my younger one – matcha , ramen, K-pop and, eventually, Korean dramas. What began as reluctant viewing has turned into a full-blown indulgence. What do you mean a good romantic K-drama can regulate my nervous system ?
 While the rest of the world seems to be in a rush to fast-forward romance , K-dramas understand the delicious art of making you yearn for the yearners on screen. A lingering glance, an almost-confession, the tiniest brush of a pinkie finger. Sometimes, the anticipation is the whole point. And we're perfectly happy spending the first 15 episodes waiting for it.
 On the other hand, I have an equally soft spot for a gripping crime thriller or horror series , particularly one that can make me put my phone down and stop doomscrolling while watching TV (don't come for me, I know we're all guilty of it). So, if you're already a K-drama devotee but haven't had the time to sift through November's releases, consider this your watchlist shortcut. We've cherry-picked a mix of romantic escapism, crime, suspense and everything in between, with enough variety to suit whatever mood you're in. No endless scrolling required. You're welcome.
 The Remarried Empress
 I love a plot with a scorned woman baying for blood. As Cardi B famously once put it, “I don’t take the high road; if they go low I take it to hell where the lava is at, the volcano erupted.” And honestly, this is exactly that. Starring Shin Min Ah, Ju Ji Hoon, Lee Jong Suk and Lee Se Young, The Remarried Empress follows Empress Navier, whose husband asks for a divorce, prompting her to turn around and marry the neighbouring kingdom's prince instead. Based on Alphatart's hugely popular web novel, adapted into a webtoon by HereLee and Sumpul, this royal fantasy promises palace politics, revenge and the kind of deliciously calculated comeuppance we're always rooting for.
 The Blue Road
 Romance may be the genre that gets us through the rough weeks, but crime-led K-dramas deserve a little more love on your watchlist, especially when they promise to have you hooked from the first scene. The Blue Road , featuring Son Suk Ku, Eita Nagayama, Kim Shin Rock, Choi Sung Eun and Jung Jae Young, follows a Korean detective and a Japanese detective with very different approaches to solving crimes, brought together by an investigation that crosses international borders. This is the kind of show that could have you halting mid-bite during dinner. And what do you mean two detectives with opposing methods have to find common ground to crack an international case? Add director Han Jun Hee to the mix, and we're already sold. Even better, all episodes drop together, so consider your weekend plans sorted.
 Good Partner 2
 One thing I particularly admire about K-dramas is the sheer range of professions and career settings they use to build their storylines. From lawyers and journalists to doctors and detectives, there's always a new world to get pulled into. Good Partner 2 is a case in point. The hit legal drama returns with Jang Nara reprising her role as Cha Eun Kyung , a formidable divorce lawyer navigating the messy business of marital breakdowns, this time alongside a new colleague, Kang Hye Sung , played by Kim Hye Yoon. If the first season taught us anything, it's that divorce cases are rarely just about who gets the house, the money or the children. Expect complicated clients, courtroom showdowns and enough relationship drama to make you grateful you're watching from the other side of the screen.
 Sword & Silence (Munmu)
 Period dramas are always a fascinating watch, particularly when you throw in complicated family dynamics, internal politics and enough pride and prestige to keep an entire kingdom on its toes. Sword & Silence (Munmu) , headlined by Lee Hyun Wook, Jang Hyuk, Kim Kang Woo and Park Sung Woong, takes us back to Korea's Three Kingdoms period, exploring the political power struggles and military campaigns that eventually led to the unification of the peninsula under Silla. Yes, you get to brush up on an era of Korean history you don't hear nearly enough about while being thoroughly entertained. Family rivalries, power plays, battles for the throne and a stellar veteran cast? Sign me up. History class could never.
 What a Boss Wants
 Read More I Went to Seoul and Tried Korea's Most Talked About Treatments Here's what the hype is all about
 By Keanoush Zargham What did I just say about fun professions and career settings? With Sung Hoon, Oh Se Young and CNBLUE’s Lee Jung Shin in the mix, What a Boss Wants brings together a data-driven, emotionally unavailable tech CEO, a struggling job seeker who moonlights as the lead vocalist of an indie band and a warm-hearted paediatrician. The CEO, Kwon Do Hyuk , becomes infatuated with the mysterious voice of singer Su , unaware that she is actually Lee Eun Chae , the woman behind the microphone. It might sound like a storyline we’ve seen before, complete with a double identity, an unlikely romance and a love triangle thrown in for good measure. But if there’s one thing K-dramas have taught us, it’s that good storytelling can make even the most familiar tropes worth revisiting.
 The Substitute
 Academic pressure can be the villain origin story for many students, but The Substitute takes that idea a step further by looking at how differently we play the cards we’re dealt. Because no matter how academically gifted you are, being born into a certain class can determine just how many hurdles life throws your way. With Bae Hyeon Seong, Cha Kang Yoon and Park Yoon Ho in the lead roles, this psychological crime thriller follows a wealthy but struggling student who blackmails a brilliant, low-income scholarship student into sitting the university entrance exam on his behalf. What begins as a one-day favour quickly spirals into a web of deception, secrets and shifting power dynamics. It's a premise that claws into the inequalities beneath South Korea's fiercely competitive education system, asking just how far someone might go when their future feels like it's riding on a single exam.
 One of a Kind Romance
 Red Velvet's Joy leads One of a Kind Romance , a romantic comedy that brings together an ordinary job seeker and a not-so-ordinary celebrity. Based on the popular webtoon of the same name, the K-drama follows Gong Yu Il (Joy), whose life takes an unexpected turn when she becomes the manager of top actor Tak Mu I (Kim Hyun Jin). Unbeknownst to her, Mu I happens to be the biggest fan of a novel she wrote years ago. Throw in a mysterious celebrity chef, a childhood friend turned romantic rival, and your few emotional wounds to heal – and you've got all the ingredients for a classic, feel-good K-drama romance.
